item.title: Kimi Antonelli explains mistake that left him “smoked by the two McLarens” in Vegas
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli looked primed to cap a charge from sixth on the grid with a dramatic last-lap victory at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Instead, one split-second pedal adjustment drained his battery dry - handing Max Verstappen breathing room and dropping the Mercedes driver off the podium entirely. After topping Friday qualifying before a five-place power unit penalty relegated him to sixth, Antonelli used an alternative medium-to-soft tyre strategy to slice back into contention. When team-mate George Russell locked up into the Turn 5 barrier late in the race, Antonelli stood as Verstappen’s lone remaining threat. Yet heading onto the final lap, his W17 abruptly slowed exiting the final chicane, allowing Lando Norris (+0.639 seconds) and Oscar Piastri (+1.529s from 17th on the grid) to sweep past into Turn 1. Antonelli crossed the line fourth, 2.574s behind Verstappen and just 0.353s ahead of Alpine ’s Pierre Gasly . Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Speaking afterwards to Sky Sports F1’s Craig Slater, Antonelli clarified that switching his energy deployment map was not to blame - his attempt to manage the gap behind Verstappen disrupted the car's regeneration cycle. "No, I think the change of deployment was good because it was the best option to then stay ahead after the chicane in case I was overtaking Max before Turn 14," Antonelli explained. "But because I wanted to keep the overtake mode, I lift off and reapply some throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that messed up the whole battery harvesting, and I stayed in the chicane at zero. "So I lost more than a second going into Turn 1, and not only I couldn't stay close to Max and give myself a good shot for the win, but I got smoked by the two McLarens as well and lost the podium," he added. "So probably it was a mistake on my side, but in the moment it's also very difficult because I thought I was doing something right to stay behind and keep the overtake." High-speed chess match with Verstappen The error carried an ironic twist after Antonelli spent Thursday praising Mercedes as likely the grid’s most efficient package in electrical energy management heading into power-sensitive Nevada. Across the final 15 laps, however, neither Mercedes nor Red Bull wanted to lead too early down the 1.9-kilometre Strip straight, triggering a tense game of cat and mouse over overtake mode. item.title: Fred Vasseur "more than upset" with "unacceptable" Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc Las Vegas clash
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Fred Vasseur said that Charles Leclerc's clash with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "completely unacceptable", and added he was "more than upset" that the team's message to its drivers seems to have been ignored again. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the team-mates fought over sixth place around the streets of Las Vegas. Hamilton dropped to 10th and recovered to finish seventh , while Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty and finished 10th. Speaking to Sky Sports after the race, Vasseur said the team had repeated the message it gave after Mexico. "Clearly, it's unacceptable. First, a little bit the same message as Mexico, because you have to think about the team, about the people working in Maranello, about all the stakeholders, the sponsors," he said. The team chief revealed Ferrari had spoken to Leclerc during the race, explaining that the nature of the Las Vegas track meant its drivers had to focus on the cars around them. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake, because in this kind of race, as you were saying before, you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you are passed by the others. It means that you have to do your race," he continued. "And Charles, it's clearly a mistake that is penalising the team a lot. And it's completely unacceptable today. Honestly, I'm more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico." The pair clashed on the opening lap in Mexico three weeks ago, when Leclerc was given a five-second penalty for passing Hamilton off the track. Ferrari then held talks with both drivers. "We had a chat together, all together, in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together. And the outcome is this one," Vasseur said. "It's mega frustrating for all of us." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps, Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. item.title: Lewis Hamilton: Las Vegas penalty "really harsh" as podium chance slipped
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton says his 10-second penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "really harsh" as his chance of a podium slipped from his fingers during a chaotic race. Hamilton started 11th after both Ferraris were knocked out in Q2. He climbed quickly through the field, but was penalised for leaving the track and gaining an advantage at the Turn 7-8 chicane while battling McLaren's Lando Norris . He then lost even more of the ground he'd made up when team-mate Charles Leclerc spun him around while they fought over sixth, dropping him to 10th. Hamilton fought back to finish seventh, while Leclerc was penalised and finished 10th. "We knew that we were faced with massive challenges this weekend. We didn't realise there would be such a limitation on the straights," Hamilton told Sky Sports. "The qualifying, obviously, was difficult, but in the race I felt great, and I really was progressing well." He didn't hide how he felt about the penalty. "Then avoiding collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty, which was, I think, really harsh, which was frustrating. But I just got my head back down and just kept chasing and managed to get back in the fight," he said. "Then again, I got knocked back again. But I never gave up, and I was just trying to get the best results. I really think we could have had a podium today." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton didn't hide his feelings during the race, either. In a message not broadcast on the world feed , he hinted at the five-second penalty Leclerc was given for a similar off-track pass in Mexico, saying: "They give me 10 for avoiding an incident." Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur agreed the punishment was too harsh, saying: "Honestly, I was surprised with the 10 seconds." Hamilton would not be drawn on the collision with Leclerc, saying it was "something for you to speak to Ferrari about". Asked whether it was time for proper rules between the two Ferrari drivers after Mexico, he said: "I've done all I can, and I've said everything and more." "All I can do is just show up and give it everything I can, and hopefully in the background they'll eventually figure it out." The result moves Hamilton up to third in the drivers' standings on 267 points, three ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris, with two races to go. The former Newport and Pontypool forward, who takes over from Richard Collier-Keywood , attends his first WRU annual general meeting (AGM) on Sunday. He has already promised to review everything including the controversial plan to cut a men's professional side by 2028. Faulkner has forged a highly successful business career in the United States of America. The 66-year-old also has a Welsh rugby background as the nephew of former Wales rugby prop Charlie Faulkner, who was yesterday inducted into World Rugby's hall of fame alongside Bobby Windsor and Graham Price - the famed Pontypool front-row. item.title: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2
item.description: Messi Tops 2026 MLS Salary List at $28.3M, Lewandowski Jumps to No. 2 Lionel Messi remains Major League Soccer's highest-paid player, with $28.3 million in guaranteed compensation for 2026, according to the MLS Players Association's final salary release of the year. Robert Lewandowski, who joined Chicago Fire in June, has overtaken Son Heung-min for second place at $19.51 million. The gap at the top is still enormous. Messi's guaranteed pay is up from $20.45 million a year ago, and his individual number now runs more than double the entire Philadelphia Union roster , which carries the league's lowest total payroll at $12.64 million. Why Messi's number keeps climbing Messi signed a contract extension through the 2028 season last fall, and the new MLSPA figures reflect that deal's structure rather than a fresh negotiation. His $25 million base salary plus bonuses produces the $28.3 million guaranteed figure — and that's before factoring in revenue-sharing from Apple's MLS Season Pass and sponsorship income that Inter Miami co-owner Jorge Mas has said pushes his real annual take closer to $70-80 million. Lewandowski's arrival tells a parallel story about where MLS spending is headed. His $16 million base salary and $19.51 million guaranteed compensation make him the clearest marker yet that clubs outside Miami are now willing to commit Designated Player money at a scale that was rare even two years ago. Under MLS's salary budget rules, each Designated Player's actual salary can run far above the roster cap — only a fixed charge, $803,125 for players 24 and older, counts against a club's budget, with the team absorbing the rest. That mechanism, not the cap itself, is what makes both Messi's and Lewandowski's deals possible. What it means for the league's financial pecking order The broader numbers back up the sense that MLS wages are moving, not just at the top. Total guaranteed compensation across the league reached $724.5 million, up nearly 15% from the May release, and 150 players are now earning at least $1 million annually. Average guaranteed compensation sits at $746,936, an 18% jump year over year. Still, the hierarchy hasn't flattened — it's stretched. Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Son and Breel Embolo round out a five-player tier earning $10 million or more, but Messi sits well clear of all of them. Inter Miami's roster spending now tops the league, and the club's willingness to build around one player's market value continues to set the ceiling other front offices are chasing rather than matching. As more marquee strikers arrive mid-contract-cycle — as Lewandowski did — expect the gap between MLS's top tier and its median roster to keep widening before it narrows.

item.title: Man United’s trip to Sporting: Paulo Fonseca explains how he is preparing for Champions League tie
item.description: Man United’s trip to Sporting: Paulo Fonseca explains how he is preparing for Champions League tie Manchester United kick off the Mauricio Pochettino era with a blockbuster game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November, in the Premier League. The Red Devils are 18th in the Premier League after 10 games this season and have registered just one win in the league. The Argentine , as such, has a mini challenge at hand as he attempts to get a faltering side firing on all cylinders. Pochettino will have to make do with the options at hand until at least the January transfer window, when he could have the chance to seek squad improvements. The 54-year-old is facing a daunting task, as the team is set to play 11 times in 34 days starting on Sunday. Immediately after the Liverpool match is a trip to Portugal to face Sporting CP in the Champions League. Pochettino will be eyeing a long run in Europe United returned to the Champions League this season following a two-year absence. However, their run in Europe has hardly been convincing. The Red Devils started well, securing a 4-0 win over Sabah on Matchday One, which remains their only clean sheet across competitions this season. However, the English giants succumbed to a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid next. Things went from bad to worse in their third game in Europe’s premier club competition, with Como thrashing them 4-1. That also prompted Bruno Fernandes to publicly question former manager Michael Carrick’s tactics. United looked set for another disaster in the game against AS Roma, in which they were 2-0 behind by the 17th minute. However, the English giants fought back to secure a 3-2 win to keep hopes alive of progressing to the knockouts. The English giants are currently 17th in the table, with the top eight securing automatic qualification to the next stage, while teams from ninth to 24th have to go through play-offs. A win against Sporting next week could massively help their cause, but the Portuguese club have already begun preparations for the tie. Manchester United Champions League Results: 2026/27 Season Paulo Fonseca to watch United game against Liverpool Speaking after Saturday’s 4-0 win over União da Serra, as cited by A Bola , Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca revealed that he will keep a close watch on how United perform under Pochettino this weekend. item.description: Dynamo Kyiv 1999 GFX - Getty/GOAL No Ukrainian side has ever side won the European Cup - but Valeriy Lobanovskyi's wonderful side went close in 1999 When Valeriy Lobanovskyi faced the media after Dynamo Kyiv's Champions League semi-final second-leg loss to Bayern Munich at the Olympic Stadium in April 1999, he insisted that elimination was "no tragedy". "We are happy to have made it to the last four," he said. However, Andriy Shevchenko and the rest of his team-mates were devastated - and more for their coach than the club, the supporters or even themselves. "I hated seeing the expression on Lobanovskyi's face," the striker later wrote in his autobiography . "I could see how much he had wanted to win that trophy." And Dynamo really should have done. While everyone remembers that Bayern should have gone to beat Manchester United in the final because the nature of their injury-time collapse at Camp Nou was so unforgettable, it's often overlooked that the Bavarians were blessed to have even made it to Barcelona. Dynamo had Bayern on the ropes in the first leg of their semi in Kyiv and Lobanovskyi's wonderful side would have arguably caused Sir Alex Ferguson's United even more problems in Catalunya. After all, the Ukrainian underdogs had spent the previous two seasons upsetting Europe's elite. 'On the trail of perfection' Lobanovskyi is essentially one of the founding fathers of modern football For one of the most influential figures in football history, Lobanovskyi's name is not as well-known as it should be. The modern game simply would not be what it is today without the Ukrainian, who was very much a pioneer in terms of the use of scientific data to analyse matches and opponents. The importance he attached to team work and peak physical condition is also the stuff of legend, with Shevchenko claiming to have seen team-mates begging the coach to call off particularly punishing training sessions. He never did, though. "He was a genius," Shevchenko said , "a visionary and a subversive, perpetually on the trail of perfection." Given Lobanovskyi was also a master of psychology, players were willing to run through walls for him - which is why he managed to build two great Dynamo teams, a decade apart, in the 1970s and 80s. item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached a climax with the fixtures for the first finals weekend confirmed. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. item.title: George Russell: “I don’t regret it” after crashing out of second at Las Vegas GP
item.description: Motorsport photo George Russell could have played it safe and walked away from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix with a podium. Instead, the Mercedes driver gambled on a late lunge for second - and watched both his shot at victory and his championship cushion slide into the Turn 5 barrier. Running third on Lap 48 of 50 behind leader Max Verstappen and team-mate Kimi Antonelli, Russell locked his brakes while trying to clear Antonelli heading into Turn 5. His W17 slid nose-first into the wall, forcing him to reverse back onto the circuit and dropping him to ninth at the chequered flag - 13.192 seconds adrift of Verstappen. Even so, Russell refused to second-guess going for the win. "I knew if I wanted to win the race I needed to be in second going into the last couple of laps," Russell said. "Kimi didn’t have the overtake mode, and I just went for a high-risk move and paid the price, but I don’t regret it. Of course I’m disappointed with it, but I could have been conservative, and I would have finished in third." The miscue drew instant mockery from Verstappen - just a day after their heated FP3 clash - with the Red Bull driver laughing, "Haha, well done. My God," over team radio. Moments later, Antonelli suffered a late power deployment drop that allowed McLaren ’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri past for second and third, leaving Verstappen clear to claim his third Las Vegas win. Salvaging just two points dealt a heavy blow to Russell’s fight for runner-up honours. Verstappen jumped to 304 points - 40 clear of Russell (264) with only 50 points remaining across standard race weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi - while Ferrari ’s Lewis Hamilton (267) moved into third and Norris pulled level with Russell on 264. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes “Learning on the fly” in a wild slipstream battle Russell’s late gamble capped a frantic 50-lap tactical puzzle shaped by Formula 1’s 2026 energy-deployment rules, which triggered relentless lead swaps between Verstappen, Russell, Antonelli, and Norris. "It was interesting. It was quite fun for maybe half the race. Then it started to get a bit tiring at one point because it was absolutely impossible to get away," Russell said. "I felt I was in a very good deployment mode to overtake Verstappen and be ahead of the startline. Kimi was overtaking, but Max was already re-overtaking before the line," he added. "But it left me very vulnerable in the middle sector, and that’s why I lost some positions. I went down to P5, and then I had to change my strat mode, and it helped me get back up the order. I felt into the last lap I could go back to what I had to try and win the race. It was tough." Asked how drivers balance straight-line bursts against mid-lap exposure, Russell admitted there was no playbook. "It was just learning on the fly, really," he said. "It was very bizarre. The speed differences in the straight were monumental. I was gaining 1.3s on the straight on Max; it was wild. Strange race." To read

item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Scott McTominay continued his remarkable scoring streak against Torino with a clinical winner that earned injury-hit Napoli a 1-0 Serie A victory. After Massimiliano Allegri joked that his players score when they smile, the former Manchester United midfielder quickly turned his attention to Tuesday's Champions League trip to Manchester City. McTominay strikes again to sink Torino Scott McTominay drilled home a decisive second-half winner from the edge of the box to hand injury-ravaged Napoli a hard-fought 1-0 Serie A victory over Torino. Set up by Noa Lang after the Dutchman sprinted back to halt a Zakaria Aboukhlal counter-attack, the Scotland international buried his shot into the far bottom corner to extend his prolific record against Torino to four goals in just three meetings. The breakthrough sparked a lighthearted reaction from Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri, who turned to his bench and remarked: "See, they score when they smile, I told them to smile more." Speaking afterwards, McTominay echoed that upbeat mood while stressing the need to build consistency. Match-winner calls for momentum after vital victory Despite facing a stubborn Torino side who struck the crossbar through Rolando Mandragora before half-time and forced Lucas Perri into a string of saves from Matteo Politano and Rasmus Hojlund, Napoli held firm for three crucial points. "I am feeling much better," smiled McTominay when speaking to Sky Sport Italia . "It's an important goal, but more importantly we won, we had to win. I'm happy for the fans, we need to get a bit of momentum going, keep winning. In football it's about the next game, and the next game, you have to do your best. We have a team that wants to work, wants to push, and we want to win more games." Injury crisis forces early De Bruyne introduction Allegri reshuffled his depleted squad into a 3-5-2 formation amid an extensive absentee list featuring Alex Meret, Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Alessandro Buongiorno. De Bruyne immediately made his presence felt, slipping a pass through for Hojlund and later teeing up McTominay to test Perri, though his unexpected 79-minute outing added extra fatigue to veteran legs ahead of midweek action. Derby feel awaits McTominay at the Etihad Victory sends Napoli into Tuesday's Champions League clash away at Manchester City in higher spirits, even with Vergara expected to miss the trip. item.title: Wales boss Wilkinson rules out Fishlock return
item.description: Jess Fishlock scored 48 international goals in 166 games for Wales [FAW] Rhian Wilkinson says she has not considered asking Jess Fishlock to come out of retirement even though the Wales legend will be on camp for the Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway. Fishlock ended her playing career earlier this month after her Seattle Reign side lost to Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-offs. The 39-year-old played on for one final season at Reign having retired from international football in October 2025. Fishlock will be part of Wales' coaching staff for for next month's two-legged tie against the Norwegians, who visit the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later. Despite some speculation over whether Fishlock could play some part on the pitch, Wilkinson said: "I think you get retirement right when you know there's still something in you to give." The Wales boss added: "It takes years to recognise that you got it right, because you're sort of [thinking] 'oh should I have kept playing', but when you get it wrong injuries and someone else makes the decision that you're finished, that's a tough way to to end your career. "I think Jess has qualified [for Euro 2025], made history with Wales, done such a great job as well as building the game over in the US and equally so much in Wales. "[But] she's retired. Jess is here to further her technical and tactical awareness, but also for her experiences and that kind of confidence that she brings to the environment." While there will be no Fishlock, Wales will welcome back a number of experienced players from injury for the Norway games. Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway will likely not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer. The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway. item.title: Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat
item.description: Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia. The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff on Saturday, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations. Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot. Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions. However, they fell agonisingly short. "The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy. "We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard." The 46-year-old former Ospreys coach added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win. "I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again." Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks. "Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said. "So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well." Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Highs and lows of sport - Lake Dewi Lake has scored three tries in the past two internationals [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. "It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake. "Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best. "We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times." Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad. "We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain. "We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today. "We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week." Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
